title: Petrykivka painting
summary: Petrykivka is a decorative painting from central Ukraine in which flowers, berries and birds grow from single pressed strokes of a fingertip or a soft brush. Bright colours glow on a dark or pale ground, finished with fine curling lines.
howToPlay: Look at the framed picture: it shows the finished panel.
Dip the tool in a colour, then press and drag to paint. A slow, steady hand lays a fat line that thins as the paint runs out.
Follow the lit guide lines and dab the petals, leaves and berries; tap a shape to fill it where a step asks for fills.
Press Next when a step is done, and finish with the fine curls.
rules: Score: how closely your strokes follow the guide in the right colour, and how much of each shape holds the right colour.
Where the design is symmetric, an even pair of halves earns a bonus.
Paint outside the guide counts against you; undo takes back the last stroke.
Three stars need a careful, steady hand.
heritageNote: Petrykivka comes from the village of Petrykivka in central Ukraine, where women painted flowers and birds on house walls, chests and paper. Colour is pressed on with a fingertip or a soft brush, and the finest curls were once made with a cat-whisker brush.
